question: Does one rights-clear, camera-free density-wedge scan from an independently documented Ektachrome SO-368 magazine expose usable monotone channel response and scanner/process diagnostics for a later generic physical-film interpretation pilot?

source.name: March to the Moon / NASA Johnson Space Center
source.source_description: The archive states that density wedges were placed directly on film and exposed without a camera; wedge levels run from 100 percent opaque to 0 percent opaque.
source.scanner_description: Apollo film scans are described as Leica DSW700 scans at up to 200 pixels/mm and 14-bit A/D; exact file metadata remains to be audited.
source.rights_description: The source states that NASA/JSC raw scans of Apollo flight film are public domain under NASA still-image/computer-file policy; processed ASU products have separate restrictions and are excluded.
source.allowed_use: bounded internal research and reproducible derived measurement from raw scan members only; no processed ASU product use

magazine_evidence.association_status: independently documented magazine association; archive contents must still match AS07-03 and remain raw-scan evidence

acquisition.reason_resume_forbidden: The endpoint ignored a one-byte HTTP Range request and returned 200 chunked content on 2026-07-30.

forbidden_actions: fit any curve before acquisition integrity and raw-scan identity pass
treat wedge percentages as scene RGB or a digital-photo pair
claim modern Ektachrome, Velvia, stock calibration or scanner-independent response
infer process, exposure spacing, illuminant spectrum or density values absent from independent evidence
expand to further Apollo archives before this bounded pilot is adjudicated

branch_rule.source_pass: open a separately frozen parsing and monotonic-response feasibility audit only
branch_rule.source_fail: close this archive without curve fitting and retain manufacturer priors plus generic physical-inspired sensitometry

claim_ceiling: One historical SO-368 magazine-associated, camera-free density-wedge raw-scan source audit; not a digital-to-film pair, modern stock response, calibrated sensitometry, process truth, scanner independence or product promotion.
